Two papers in the library propose a preference-optimisation method that needs no reference model: **ORPO** and **SimPO**. A third, **KTO**, includes a reference-free version only as a weaker variant. Page numbers below are PDF page numbers.

### 1. ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model (Hong, Lee, Thorne, KAIST AI)
`llm/post-training/preference-learning/`
- The abstract calls it a "reference model-free monolithic odds ratio preference optimization algorithm" that removes the need for a separate preference-alignment phase (p. 1).
- It works by adding a small penalty for the disfavoured response, measured with an odds ratio, during supervised fine-tuning (SFT) (p. 1).
- Figure 2 shows ORPO aligning the model without a reference model (p. 2), and the conclusion repeats that it is "reference-free" (p. 9).
- Results: Phi-2, Llama-2 and Mistral fine-tuned with ORPO on UltraFeedback reach up to 12.20% on AlpacaEval 2.0, 66.19% on IFEval and 7.32 on MT-Bench (p. 1).

### 2. SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward (Meng, Xia, Chen, UVA / Princeton)
`llm/post-training/preference-learning/`
- It uses the average log probability of a sequence as the implicit reward. This "eliminates the need for a reference model, making it more compute and memory efficient" (p. 1; derived in §2.2, p. 3).
- It also adds a target reward margin to the Bradley-Terry objective (p. 1, p. 4).
- Results: it beats DPO by up to 6.4 points on AlpacaEval 2 and up to 7.5 on Arena-Hard (p. 1).
- It calls ORPO "a recent reference-free objective" and compares against it (p. 2).

### Partial case: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
- Standard KTO uses a reference model. The paper also tests a memory-saving variant that assumes the reference model gives a uniform distribution over outputs. It says "KTO works without a reference model or SFT, but not as well as standard KTO" (p. 8; the "no π_ref" ablation is on p. 18).
- So it offers a reference-free option, but that is not its main contribution.

The DPO survey in the same folder (*A Comprehensive Survey of Direct Preference Optimization*) sorts DPO variants into reference-based and reference-free groups (p. 9). The reward-model survey lists ORPO and SimPO among the reference-free methods (p. 5).
